chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'ed Abady quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of Abil Jo'aza al-Monabat ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Alvan, on the authority of Amr ibn Khalid, on the authority of Zayd ibn Ali, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them), who said:

The fur garment, shoes, hat, cloak, turban, and underwear are removed from the martyr's body, unless his underwear is bloody in which case it is not taken off. And anything tied or fastened on him is untied, except for that.
ai.seo_question: What garments and items are removed or kept with a martyr's body during burial according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal details the specific ritual practice of removing outer garments and accessories from a martyr before burial, preserving only the undergarments if stained with blood as a sign of their sacrifice. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of distinguishing the burial rites of martyrs from the general deceased, emphasizing purity and the unique status of the shahid. The instruction to untie all fastenings ensures the body is prepared for the afterlife without impediment, aligning with the broader Islamic emphasis on simplicity and readiness for divine judgment.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 6-33 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa’ed Abady quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of Abil Jo’aza al-Monabat ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Alvan, on the authority of Amr ibn Khalid, on the authority of Zayd ibn Ali, on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), on the authority of Ali (MGB), “

They take off the fur garment, shoes, hat, cloak, turban and the underwear from the martyr’s body, unless his underwear is bloody in which case it is not taken off. Then they unbutton any buttons or unzip zippers and bury him.”
